findings.title: Call to undefined no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: The changed condition invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only method defined in UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so this call cannot be resolved and the module fails to compile. The call probably should pass context.getUser(), or a no-arg overload must be added.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer filled when no user is set
findings.body: authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false when context.getUser() is null. On the normal first-factor username/password page, the user is not set yet, so webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is skipped and the WebAuthn/passkey form is absent. Previously this code filled the passkey form for that case. The challenge(...) override at line 137 has the same condition, so passkeys also disappear after an invalid username or password submission. Existing passkey tests such as passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey expect the webauth form at these stages.

findings.title: Re-authentication enables passkey UI regardless of whether the user has a passkey
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) only checks that passkeys are enabled for the realm and that user is non-null. During re-authentication it causes fillContextForm to be called even for a user with no WebAuthn passwordless credential. Such users get a passkey option that cannot succeed and may produce WebAuthn errors. The check should also verify the user has a configured passwordless credential, for example via user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS).
